view_frame: The drawing uses third-angle projection with three views: BOTTOM (XY plane), TOP (XY plane), and FRONT (XZ plane). The world coordinate system is defined with X as width (left-right), Y as depth (front-back), and Z as height (vertical). The FRONT view displays the object's profile in the XZ plane, showing the transition from the rectangular base to the circular top.

features.placement: The solid is centered on the XY origin. The bottom profile is a rectangle (60mm width in X, 40mm depth in Y) located at Z=0. The top profile is a circle (30mm diameter) located at Z=60. The loft connects these two profiles linearly.
features.evidence: BOTTOM view shows a '60 x 40 mm rectangle'. TOP view shows a 'diameter 30 mm' circle. FRONT view shows a trapezoidal profile labeled 'height 60 mm; solid'.

connections: The rectangular base (60x40) and circular top (diameter 30) are connected by a linear loft along the Z-axis.
edit_rules: Changing the rectangle width (X) or depth (Y) updates the bottom profile of the loft.
Changing the circle diameter updates the top profile of the loft.
Changing the height updates the Z-separation between the two profiles.
The loft maintains a straight transition between the rectangular and circular sections.
